svg.text: One headline rate hides several stories
Bureau of Labor Statistics data: race, age, education and the broader U-6 measure.
A Black–White gap that has held for 50 years
Black rate ÷ White rate each year: 2.1× on average, 1.9× in 2026.
2-to-1 or more in 36 of 54 years; never under 1.5-to-1.
2024 unemployment: White (teal) vs Black (orange); right = Black ÷ White.
What the official rate leaves out
U-6 minus U-3, in points. In 2026: U-3 4.25%, U-6 7.98%.
Teenagers carry several times the adult rate
BLS CPS & LAUS · seasonally adjusted · U-6 starts 1994 (CPS redesign) · teen rate is a share of the labor force, not of all teens.
